newSounds: Three throaty consonants English and Telugu lack: x = kh (harsh h, like Scottish loch), q = gh (a French-r sound from the back of the throat), and zh = zh (as in measure). Also sh = sh, ch as in cheese, and a quick glottal stop marked '.
rhythm: Syllable-timed, close to Telugu's even beat. Every vowel is its own syllable (CV, CVC, CVCC). Stress usually falls on the last syllable of a word; enclitics such as -am, -id, -ra do not move it.
registerFirst: Polite shoma first, with -id verb endings and -etan for 'your'; the informal to with -i endings is for friends and family. Use befarmayid to invite someone in and bebakhshid to get attention politely.
trap: The ezafe link -e (or -ye after a vowel) ties a noun to what follows (hal-e shoma = your state; mah-e ayande = next month) and is said as a light, unstressed 'e'. Never read the Persian script aloud: short vowels are not written, so the spoken form must be learned separately from the literary form.
